newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Surgical sees sales accelerating.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Surgical sees sales accelerating.

text.p: U.S. Surgical Corp chairman Leon Hirsch said on Tuesday he expects the company's sales to accelerate much more quickly in 1997 than they have in the past year.

Presenting the company's new products in San Francisco, Hirsch said: "I do expect our sales to accelerate at a much more rapid rate than they have in the past year in 1997 and a hell of a lot more in 1998."
He declined to give a percentage figure.

In July, the company reported net profits of $0.66 per share on sales of $549.6 million in the six months ended June 30, compared with earnings of $0.42 per share on sales of $504.2 million in the same period a year earlier.

Hirsch said U.S. Surgical was targeting selling, general and administrative costs next year to be at least two percentage points lower than this year. "We want to be under 40 percent. I think that's an absolutely achievable number," he said.

Hirsch spoke as U.S. Surgical introduced what it called the world's first full set of instruments for minimally invasive coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery at the American College of Surgeons meeting in San Francisco.

The company also unveiled an extensive array of other new products and approaches for prostate surgery, orthopaedics, vascular stenosis, fibrin adhesives, cancer detection, ultrasonics and wound products.
The Mini-CABG instruments will allow surgeons to operate on a beating heart through a three to four inch incision instead of the usual 12-inch incision.
The entire set of Mini-CABG instruments -- except for a clamp -- has already been cleared for marketing by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and will be launched in January.

"We are very excited about entering the cardiovascular market. I believe our instruments are the first to solve many of the problems facing surgeons today when performing minimally invasive CABG procedures," Hirsch said.

U.S. Surgical also unveiled a new technology, called the Radio Frequency Therapy system, for treating benign prostate hyperplasia, an enlargement of the prostate that constricts the urethra, making urination difficult.
